name: Hotel de la Cite Carcassonne
positioning: Hotel de la Cite, a historic hotel and former bishop's residence in the heart of Carcassonne's UNESCO-listed medieval Cite, next to the Basilica of Saint-Nazaire, with gardens, a Cinq Mondes spa and a heated outdoor pool
best_for: Travelers who want to stay inside Carcassonne's medieval Cite
Couples looking for a historic hotel with a spa and garden pool

facts.text: The hotel is in the heart of Carcassonne's medieval Cite, built on the site of the former episcopal palace and next to the Basilica of Saint-Nazaire.
The historic hotel, a former bishop's residence, has wood paneling, coats of arms and lush gardens, with a view over the lower town of Carcassonne.
The reception area and lounges mix neo-Gothic decor with the Art Deco spirit of the 1920s.
Most of the neo-Gothic building dates to 1909.
The heated outdoor pool sits in the hotel's gardens at the foot of the Basilica of Saint-Nazaire, with a summer bar in fine weather.
The spa offers Cinq Mondes treatments and adjoins the hotel's heated outdoor pool.
The spa has an experience shower with three water-treatment programmes.
The spa has a phyto-aromatic bath and a duo treatment room.
Superior rooms are doubles with a garden view and a private bathroom with a bathtub.
The Suite has a king-size bed, a separate living room with a sofa bed and a marble bathroom with a bathtub.
At La Barbacane, Chef Jerome Ryon and pastry chef Regis Chanel focus on traditional cuisine renewed with refinement and subtlety.
The Boulangerie de la Cite is set in one of the oldest corbelled houses of the fortress, dating from the late 15th century, facing the Basilica of Saint-Nazaire.

highlights.text: The hotel stands in the heart of the medieval Cite of Carcassonne, a UNESCO World Heritage site, right beside the Basilica of Saint-Nazaire.
The spa's relaxation area opens directly onto the pool and has a whirlpool bath with aromatherapy using personalised essential oils.
In fine weather the Bar Bibliotheque moves into the hotel gardens, onto a terrace facing the fortress ramparts and the Chateau Comtal.
Bathrooms use marble from nearby quarries, and some have the same reddish marble used at Le Petit Trianon at Versailles.
An intimate garden offers a peaceful retreat in the heart of the medieval Cite.

considerations.text: Apart from small staff cars, the interior of the citadel is pedestrianized.
The outdoor pool is seasonal, open for swimming from May to the end of October.
WhataHotel notes that heritage building constraints limit some modern amenities.
